newsitem.title: UK: BOXING-TIME FOR PRINCE NASEEM TO HEAD WEST.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-TIME FOR PRINCE NASEEM TO HEAD WEST.

text.p: The flamboyant "Prince" Naseem Hamed has comprehensively conquered the featherweight division in his native Britain. Now he must look to the Americas.
Hamed's 93-second demolition of compatriot Billy Hardy on Saturday night in defence of his WBO and IBF featherweight titles was his 26th straight victory in what is becoming a remarkable career.
Twenty-four of those triumphs have been inside the distance -- 21 of them within the first six rounds.

But while his punching power, fluid movement in the ring, trademark leopard-skin shorts, celebratory somersaults and outspoken self-confidence have made "Naz" a big hit in Britain and in Yemen, the birthplace of his parents, he has still to truly make his mark on the rest of the world.

His impressive eighth round victory over American Tommy "Boom Boom" Johnson in February raised a few eyebrows in the United States but, although he has dealt uncompromisingly with everything thrown at him in Britain, the self-styled Prince has yet to fight overseas.
A challenge to WBA champion Wilfredo Vasquez of Puerto Rico -- possibly in a high-profile clash in Las Vegas later this year -- appears to be his next priority.
"I'm ready for Vasquez, to bring some more belts home to (home town) Sheffield," Hamed said after Saturday's one-sided contest in which he twice knocked Hardy to the canvas.
"I knew it would happen in the first round. Once I hit him with this amazing power that Allah, that God, gave me, it's untrue. You're going to get knocked out. Full stop.
"You saw it for yourselves: the power, the accuracy, the skill. You can't test a gift from God."
Hamed can be sure that Vasquez will test that gift to the full, as will Luisito Espinoza of the Philippines, the current holder of the WBC featherweight belt.
But the Prince, still only 23, is determined to fulfil his dream of unifying all four belts before perhaps moving up a grade to join the super-featherweights.
The hapless Hardy, who Hamed only deigned to fight because he was forced to by the World Boxing Organisation (WBO), was left in no doubt the Prince could become king of the featherweight world.

"He's got a kick like a mule...and I feel in my heart of hearts that he's going on to be the four-time champion because he's got that knock-out punch," the 32-year-old European champion said as he came to terms with his crushing defeat.
"I honestly feel that he's got something special in his hands. If he can hit me like that he can unify anything."
